claims.claim: promptarena runs one scenario against multiple LLM providers and reports each provider's responses for comparison
Supported provider types include OpenAI, Claude (anthropic) and Gemini
Tutorial 1 exists at /arena/tutorials/01-first-test/
OpenAI API keys are issued at platform.openai.com/api-keys
Anthropic console is at console.anthropic.com
Gemini API keys are issued at aistudio.google.com/app/apikey
OPENAI_API_KEY is the env var read for the openai provider
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is the env var read for the anthropic provider
GOOGLE_API_KEY is the env var read for the gemini provider
Provider manifests use apiVersion promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1
Provider manifest kind is Provider
metadata.name is a valid provider name field
metadata.labels is a valid field and accepts provider label
spec.type accepts the value openai
spec.model is a valid field and gpt-4o-mini is an accepted model value
spec.defaults is a valid object field of a provider
spec.defaults.temperature is a valid field of type float
spec.defaults.max_tokens is a valid snake_case field of type int
spec.type accepts the value anthropic
claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022 is an accepted anthropic model value
spec.type accepts the value gemini
gemini-1.5-flash is an accepted gemini model value
Scenario manifest kind is Scenario with apiVersion promptkit.altairalabs.ai/v1alpha1
metadata.name and metadata.labels are valid scenario metadata fields
spec.task_type is a valid scenario field and accepts support
spec.turns is a list of turn objects
turns[].role accepts user
turns[].content is a valid string field
turns[].assertions is a valid per-turn list field
content_includes is a registered assertion type
content_includes takes params.patterns as a list
patterns is the list of strings the content must include
params.message is a valid assertion field used as the failure message
content_matches is a registered assertion type
content_matches takes params.pattern as a regex
content_includes params.patterns is accepted in turn 2 of a scenario
Arena manifest kind is Arena
metadata.name is a valid arena field
spec.prompt_configs is a valid list field
prompt_configs entries have an id field
prompt_configs entries have a file field and prompts/support.yaml is a file path the reader creates
spec.providers is a list of entries each with a file field
spec.scenarios is a list of entries each with a file field
promptarena run is a valid command
promptarena run with no provider flag runs tests across all providers listed in the arena file
run prints the banner 'PromptArena Starting...'
run prints 'Loaded 1 prompt config' for one prompt_configs entry
run prints the loaded provider names: openai-gpt4o-mini, claude-sonnet, gemini-flash
run prints 'Loaded 1 scenario'
run reports 6 test executions for 3 providers x 1 scenario x 2 turns
run result lines name the scenario 'Product Inquiry'; the scenario in this page is named customer-support
run result lines print the provider name in square brackets and the turn elapsed time in seconds
run prints a 'Results by Provider' summary with passed counts and percentages
run prints 'Overall: N/N passed (P%)'
promptarena run accepts --format with value markdown
the markdown report is written to out/results.md
the markdown report shows side-by-side provider results
promptarena serve is a valid command
promptarena serve offers an interactive view with filtering and conversation detail
promptarena run accepts --provider with a single provider name
promptarena run --provider accepts a comma-separated list of provider names
promptarena run accepts --scenario with a scenario name
--scenario style-test selects the scenario whose metadata.name is style-test
promptarena run accepts --format json
scenarios/style-test.yaml is a scenario with metadata.name style-test and spec.task_type support
content_matches pattern ^.{50,500}$ is a valid regex accepted by the assertion
out/results.json is written by --format json
the JSON output has a top-level results array whose entries have provider and response fields
Response times are reported per result
a scenario with only a non-empty content_matches assertion checks response times
pricing table: gpt-4o-mini input $0.15 and output $0.60 per 1M tokens
pricing table: claude-3-5-sonnet input $3.00 and output $15.00 per 1M tokens
pricing table: gemini-1.5-flash input $0.075 and output $0.30 per 1M tokens
promptarena run accepts --format json
results entries have provider and response_time fields
the jq block computes costs
labels accepts a provider-specific: openai key (free label)
is_valid_json is a registered assertion type
is_valid_json accepts params.message
spec.description is a valid scenario field
content_includes patterns list accepts the value 'key points'
spec.defaults.temperature 0.7 and max_tokens 500 are valid defaults
spec.defaults.temperature 0.9 is a valid value
spec.defaults.temperature 0.1 is a valid value
the 'Avoid' example (patterns under assertions with no type) is a valid assertion
promptarena run --provider accepts comma-separated names openai-creative and openai-precise
metadata.annotations.notes is a valid scenario metadata field
Claude tends to be more verbose; OpenAI is more concise and Gemini the fastest
OPENAI_API_KEY is read by the openai provider
ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is read by the anthropic provider
GOOGLE_API_KEY is read by the gemini provider
promptarena config-inspect is a valid command
config-inspect lists all configured providers
promptarena run accepts --concurrency with an integer value
promptarena run --provider openai-gpt4o-mini runs only that provider
Tutorial 3 exists at /arena/tutorials/03-multi-turn/
Tutorial 4 exists at /arena/tutorials/04-mcp-tools/
How-to configure-providers page exists at /arena/how-to/providers/configure-providers/
Azure OpenAI and Groq can be added as provider types
Tutorial 3 covers multi-turn conversations that maintain context across exchanges
